title: The Ripe apple on the tree
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：ripe　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 ripe 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the coach wrote of ① a ripe apple on the tree in the record, and everybody in the field said at once that it was ② riper than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the coach, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the ripe ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the ripest apple on the tree anybody in the field had ever seen, or so the record for April 1948 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too ripe to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the player who had come to help; the ripe ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the whistle at the far stand, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a ripe moment for the change, and said that no player in his right mind would call it ⑥ as ripe as the moment for the change they had once had in the old field. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was ripe or not, and he said so.

By 1961 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the record. What the line asked for was ⑦ something ripe, and nothing besides. The player from the next field called the whole plan ⑧ quite ripe; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the record kept the names of the ripe ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1964, twice over, she wrote of another ripe apple on the tree in the same record, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ riper than anybody had expected. ⑩ The ripest moment for the change in the whole field, she said in 1966, was the one she could never quite name; the ripe ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 熟透（前置定语 a ripe apple on the tree：1954 年教练在赛事记录里记下的那件熟透的苹果）
B. adj. 熟透／时机成熟（比较级 riper than：文中两处，一处比树上熟透的苹果，一处比预想）
C. adj. 熟透／时机成熟（最高级 the ripest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 熟透（表语 too ripe to do：母亲觉得它太熟透，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 时机成熟（前置定语 a ripe moment for the change：叔叔把整件事称作一桩时机成熟的时机）
F. adj. 时机成熟（同级比较 as ripe as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩变革成熟的时机相比）
G. adj. 时机成熟（后置定语 something ripe：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 时机成熟（受程度副词修饰 quite ripe：那位队员的评价）

items.q: a ripe apple on the tree
the ripest apple on the tree anybody
a ripe moment for the change
The ripest moment for the change in

answers.why: ripe 意为“熟透”，1954 年教练在赛事记录里记下的是“一件熟透的苹果”，此处作前置定语 a ripe apple on the tree。
ripe 意为“熟透”，此处用比较级 riper than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
ripe 意为“熟透”，赛事记录上 四月 那行字说它是球场里最熟透的一件，故用最高级 the ripest apple on the tree。
ripe 意为“熟透”，母亲认为这件东西“太熟透了，谁也用不上”，too ripe to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
ripe 意为“时机成熟”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩时机成熟的时机”，此处作前置定语 a ripe moment for the change。
ripe 意为“时机成熟”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩变革成熟的时机一样时机成熟”，同级比较用 as ripe as。
ripe 意为“时机成熟”，赛事记录上那半行字要的是“时机成熟的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something ripe。
ripe 意为“时机成熟”，邻球场来的那位队员认为这套计划“相当时机成熟”，quite 修饰原级 ripe。
ripe 意为“时机成熟”，1964 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要时机成熟”，故用比较级 riper than。
ripe 意为“时机成熟”，母亲 1966 年说的是“整个球场里最时机成熟的那一桩”，故用最高级 the ripest moment for the change。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1954 年，教练在赛事记录里记下了一件熟透的苹果。（a ripe apple on the tree）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更熟透。（riper than …）
母亲觉得它太熟透，谁也用不上。（too ripe to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩时机成熟的时机。（a ripe moment for the change）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩变革成熟的时机一样时机成熟。（as ripe as …）
到了 1961 年，赛事记录上只剩半行字：要的是一件时机成熟的东西。（something ripe）
answers: In 1954 the coach wrote of a ripe apple on the tree in the record.
Everybody said it was riper than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too ripe to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a ripe moment for the change.
He said nobody would call it as ripe as the moment for the change they had once had.
By 1961 the record asked for nothing but something ripe.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 ripe 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1954 the coach wrote of a ripe apple on the tree in the record, and nobody forgot it.
It was the ripest apple on the tree in the field, or so the record says.
My mother thought it too ripe to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a ripe moment for the change, and nobody argued with him.
The player from the next field called the plan quite ripe, and everybody laughed.
The ripe ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
